To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a dense CGO interlayer with a grain size of d 90 < 1 μm is required to obtain high power densities with an LSCF-type cathode.
the electrochemical performance is strongly affected by the microstructure and the composition of the CGO layer, and can be improved by sputtered interlayer deposition.
the use of a CGO interlayer is essential in order to benefit from the excellent electrochemical properties of LSCF cathodes in SOFCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a cathode material for SOFCs, which can be applied to anode-supported cells without the need of an expensive diffusion barrier layer.
the development of ferrite-based cathode materials for SOFC applications, which can be used with YSZ electrolytes and which are compatible with conventional fabrication processes.
the development of ferrite-based perovksites as cathode material for anode-supported SOFCs, and with the development of interlayers for the use of these materials in anode-supported SOFCS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the electrochemical performance is improved by a sintered interlayer with a fine powder and a sintering temperature of 1250 ° C, while a dense interlayer is beneficial with respect to chemical stability.
a fine-grained CGO interlayer is needed to prevent undesired reactions between YSZ electrolytes and LSCF cathodes.
sputter-deposited CGO interlayers are the preferred solution for the use of LSCF peroveskites as cathode material in SOFCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a CGO interlayer is a suitable approach to prevent chemical degradation of the YSZ electrolyte and to improve the electrochemical properties of LSCF cathodes in SOFCs.
the use of a CGO interlayer with a mean particle diameter of d 50 <0.5 μm and sputter-deposited at 400 °C results in a high performance of anode-supported SOFCs with LSCF cathodes.
the electrochemical performance is not only dependent on the cathode composition, as shown in part I [A. Mai et al., ibid., pp. 1341–1349], but also on the properties of the CGO layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a CGO interlayer with a fine powder and sintered or deposited at high temperatures is necessary for the application of LSCF-based SOFCs.
it is possible to obtain high power densities with LSCF-type materials in SOFCs with YSZ electrolytes, even without the use of a diffusion barrier.
the use of a thin, dense CGO interlayer is a promising approach to prevent chemical reactions between the YSZ electrolyte and the LSCF cathode.
